- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: if model shows sharp upward trend after a peak, correct by adding a downward bias of 1-2% per 3-5 day window.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.2–0.8), model often fails to capture true volatility; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean to anchor forecast.
- Forecasts with sentiment history showing “recovery” (e.g., -0.2 → +0.6) often lag true rebound; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual turn.
- Avoid forecasting 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.4 or more in 3 consecutive days) — use 15d or 21d as safer horizon.
